newsitem.title: USA: BAB Holdings sees benefit from new units.
newsitem.headline: BAB Holdings sees benefit from new units.

text.p: BAB Holdings Inc said Friday its fiscal 1997 results will benefit from a full year of operation of Big Apple Bagel units opened during fiscal 1996, as well as from the February 1996 acquisition of Brewster's Coffee and new licensing agreements.

The company said groundwork was laid in fiscal 1996 to develop BAB's three principal growth drivers -- Big Apple Bagels, Brewster's Coffee and non-traditional licensing. That, in addition to the potential for additional acquisitions, positions the company for significantly increased revenues and improved profitability, BAB said.
BAB currently has 162 bagel store units, including 22 company-owned stores.

"In addition to our plans for future expansion, the seven company-owned stores added during the last four months of fiscal 1996 hold the potential for substantial growth in revenues for BAB in fiscal 1997," Michael Evans, president, said in a statement. "BAB incurred most of the start-up costs related to these stores in fiscal 1996, and the stores are expected to reach full production during fiscal 1997."

Earlier, BAB reported a loss for fiscal 1996 of $0.04 a share, including $651,000 in uncompleted acquisition costs, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.13 a share. Revenues rose to $6.3 million from $2.0 million.

"In fiscal 1996, BAB's revenues more than tripled, but the costs of an uncompleted acquisition more than offset our earnings for the year," Evans said. "Nonetheless, fiscal 1997 is shaping up as a promising year as we continue to expand internally and through acquisitions, and generate a full year of results from new Big Apple Bagel units, Brewster's Coffee and non-traditional licensing."
